boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Randolph-Macon spaces with documented study, recreation, arts, research, or student-engagement uses.

cards.title: McGraw-Page Library
cards.subtitle: Research, study, and collaboration
cards.notes: Choose a floor to match the task: use the first-floor service hub or reserve a study room before a group project.
cards.short_summary: A multi-use academic home with research help, technology, and varied study seating.
cards.evidence_claim: The library provides space for research, study, and collaboration, including reservable study rooms and both individual and group seating.
cards.source_title: McGraw-Page Library | Randolph-Macon College Academic Catalog
cards.access_notes: Library services are described for Randolph-Macon students; confirm visitor access with the library.

cards.title: Abernathy Room
cards.subtitle: McGraw-Page Library’s 24/7 study space
cards.notes: Use this named library room when you need a round-the-clock study setting; bring what you need and follow library rules.
cards.short_summary: A 24/7 study room with a printer, vending machines, and restrooms.
cards.evidence_claim: The Abernathy Room provides 24/7 study space and includes a printer, vending machines, and restrooms.
cards.source_title: McGraw-Page Library | Randolph-Macon College Academic Catalog
cards.access_notes: Documented as student study space; access may require an RMC ID.

cards.title: Make a prototype at the library
cards.subtitle: First floor, McGraw-Page Library
cards.notes: Ask Instructional Design & Technology about support before planning a build, then use the available tools for an academic project.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor makerspace with fabrication and immersive-technology tools.
cards.evidence_claim: Instructional Design & Technology supports a first-floor makerspace with 3D printers, virtual reality, a laser cutter, Legos, and more.
cards.source_title: McGraw-Page Library | Randolph-Macon College Academic Catalog
cards.access_notes: Library-based academic resource; ask staff about current availability and training.

cards.title: J. Rives Childs Room
cards.subtitle: Evening and weekend study in McGraw-Page Library
cards.notes: Plan an evening or weekend session here when it is not being used for daytime instruction or staff meetings.
cards.short_summary: A library instruction room that becomes a student study space outside daytime uses.
cards.evidence_claim: The J. Rives Childs Room is available evenings and weekends as a student study space.
cards.source_title: McGraw-Page Library | Randolph-Macon College Academic Catalog
cards.access_notes: Availability is limited by daytime library instruction and staff meetings.

cards.title: Trace a campus story in the archives
cards.subtitle: Second floor, McGraw-Page Library
cards.notes: Start with a focused research question, then contact library staff about using archival materials and special collections.
cards.short_summary: The library’s second-floor home for College Archives and distinctive research collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Special Collections and Archives is on the library’s second floor and houses the College Archives and collections including Virginia Methodism, Casanova, and Henry Miller.
cards.source_title: McGraw-Page Library | Randolph-Macon College Academic Catalog
cards.access_notes: Consult library staff for access to archival and special-collection materials.

cards.title: Student Engagement Center
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Brock Commons
cards.notes: Stop in to connect a club idea, service project, event plan, or leadership question with the staff and student resources there.
cards.short_summary: The student-life hub for clubs, service, leadership, inclusion, and campus programming.
cards.evidence_claim: The SEC in Brock Commons supports student organizations, service projects, leadership programming, inclusion, residence life, and major events.
cards.access_notes: Located in Brock Commons on the second floor; contact the SEC for meetings or program support.

cards.title: Brock Sports and Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: Fitness, aquatics, courts, and intramurals
cards.notes: Bring your RMC ID and choose an activity that fits the day, from indoor track laps to recreation-center courts or aquatics.
cards.short_summary: A 74,000-square-foot campus recreation facility with varied indoor and outdoor activity spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The Brock Center includes a pool, indoor track, fitness center, climbing wall, multipurpose courts, and staff-managed intramurals.
cards.source_title: Brock Sports and Recreation Center - Randolph-Macon College
cards.access_notes: Entry requires a valid RMC ID card or director’s pass; guests must register and may pay a fee.

cards.title: Keeble Observatory
cards.subtitle: Connected to Copley Science Center
cards.notes: Check the observatory’s weather-dependent public-viewing update before heading over, or contact the department to arrange a group visit.
cards.short_summary: A teaching and research observatory with weekly semester public viewing when conditions permit.
cards.evidence_claim: Keeble Observatory is used for student and faculty research and is open weekly during the semester for weather-dependent public viewing.
cards.access_notes: No RSVP is required for weekly public viewing, but confirm weather conditions first; group visits require scheduling.

cards.title: Blackwell Auditorium
cards.subtitle: Center for the Performing Arts
cards.notes: Look for a performance or campus arts event, and use the venue as a starting point for following RMC music and theatre programming.
cards.short_summary: A renovated 630-seat auditorium that has hosted RMC performances since the 1950s.
cards.evidence_claim: Blackwell Auditorium is part of the Center for the Performing Arts, seats 630, and has hosted RMC performances since the 1950s.
cards.access_notes: Event access and ticketing vary; consult the college calendar or event organizer.

cards.title: Brown Fountain Plaza
cards.subtitle: Central campus gathering space
cards.notes: Use the plaza as a campus meet-up point or pause between commitments; check the event calendar when major community programming is scheduled.
cards.short_summary: A named campus plaza used as a meeting point for college events and tours.
cards.evidence_claim: Randolph-Macon’s 2025 orientation schedule designated Fountain Plaza for the Official RMC Welcome, and the college’s Homecoming schedule used Brown Fountain Plaza as a campus-tour meeting location.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor plaza; access and event setup may change for scheduled college programs.
